definition: MLflow tracks experiments, packages models and manages a model registry; newer versions add tracing and evaluation for LLM apps.
details: Created by Databricks (Matei Zaharia and team) in 2018; a Linux Foundation project.

explainer.lead: How to install MLflow, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

install.javascript: npm install mlflow-tracing   # tracing for JS/TS LLM apps

quickstart.python:
import mlflow

mlflow.set_experiment("prompt-tuning")
with mlflow.start_run():
    mlflow.log_param("temperature", 0.2)
    mlflow.log_metric("accuracy", 0.91)
# view runs:  mlflow ui

explainer.inAi: Compare fine-tuning runs, version the best model, and trace each step of an LLM agent.

tiers.eli5: It's like a lab notebook plus a shipping department: it records every experiment you run and keeps each finished model labelled and stored.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to log experiment runs, package models into a reusable form and register versions for deployment; for LLM apps the newer tracing and evaluation features add oversight. A pitfall is that experiment tracking alone is not a registry — you still need the registry step to govern which model version ships.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source platform for experiment tracking, model packaging and a model registry, extended with tracing and evaluation for LLM apps. Created by Databricks (Matei Zaharia and team) in 2018; a Linux Foundation project.

explainer.example: A team logs twenty training runs, packages the best model and promotes it in the registry as the production version.
